commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

agents.name: Explore
agents.description: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions.

agents.description: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you.

tools.name: send_file
tools.title: Send file
tools.description: Deliver files to the user inside MAWS; without this tool, write the file and tell the user its path. Each delivered file becomes a row in the MAWS transcript with your caption and buttons to open it or reveal it in Finder; use it when you have produced something the user should look at (a PDF, an HTML page, an image, a document). Paths may be absolute or relative to the working directory and must name existing files. Returns the deliverable ids MAWS recorded.

tools.name: ask
tools.title: Ask questions
tools.description: Ask the user one or several questions at once through a MAWS sheet; without this tool, use AskUserQuestion. Each question has a modality: "choice" (options, single or multi, with an Other row), "text" (free text), "file" or "folder" (a native picker returning absolute paths), or "repository" (one of the user's MAWS projects). The user may answer any question with "decide for me" or skip it. With blocking true (the default) the call waits for the answers and returns them; with blocking false it returns {status: "asked", askId} at once and the answers arrive later as a user message that names the askId, so you can keep working meanwhile.

tools.name: show_pane
tools.title: Show pane
tools.description: Open a MAWS pane for the user: "diff", "file", "terminal", "tasks", "deliverable", "browser" or "source-control"; without this tool, describe where the user should look. target names what to open: a file path for diff or file (line optional), a deliverable id for deliverable, a URL for browser. Returns what was opened, or an error for an unknown pane or a pane this build of MAWS does not have.

tools.name: artifact_create
tools.title: Create artifact
tools.description: Register a self-contained HTML file you wrote as a MAWS artifact the user can view and comment on; without this tool, write the HTML file and tell the user its path. Give it a short id you will reuse for updates, the path of the HTML file (absolute or relative to the working directory) and a title. MAWS copies the file, keeps every version, shows it in a sandboxed frame with no network access (inline everything: styles, scripts, images as data URLs) and reports how many external URLs it found. Returns the artifact's deliverable id and version 1.

tools.name: artifact_update
tools.title: Update artifact
tools.description: Add a new version of a MAWS artifact from an HTML file you rewrote; without this tool, write the HTML file and tell the user its path. Names the artifact by the id you gave artifact_create; the user can switch between versions, and a title replaces the artifact's title. Returns the new version number.

tools.name: artifact_list
tools.title: List artifacts
tools.description: List the artifacts this session registered with MAWS, with their ids, titles and version counts; without this tool, keep your own list of the HTML files you wrote.

tools.name: artifact_screenshot
tools.title: Screenshot artifact
tools.description: Capture a PNG screenshot of a MAWS artifact as the user sees it, rendered in a sandboxed frame with no network; without this tool, describe the page from its source. Names the artifact by id and optionally a version (the latest by default) and a viewport size (1280 by 800 by default). Returns the image and the console errors the page logged while loading, so you can check your work.

tools.name: browser_tabs
tools.title: Browser tabs
tools.description: List, open, close or select this session's tabs in the MAWS browser; without this tool, ask the user to open the page and describe what you need from it. "list" returns the session's tabs with their ids, URLs, titles and who controls each; "open" takes a url (http or https) and opens it in a new tab that stays open until you close it; "close" and "select" take a tabId. Tabs the user opened are listed too; the user sees the tab you act on. Returns the tab list and, for open, the new tab's id.

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.title: Browser navigate
tools.description: Navigate a MAWS browser tab to a URL, or go back, forward or reload; without this tool, ask the user to open the page. url is an http or https URL or one of "back", "forward", "reload" (reload also loads a tab the user left unloaded). Waits for the page to load (up to 30 s). A page that starts a download is refused: the user downloads files, you do not. Returns the tab's URL and title after the load.

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.title: Browser snapshot
tools.description: Read a MAWS browser tab as an accessibility snapshot with element refs; without this tool, ask the user to describe the page or paste its text. Each interactive or named element has a ref like e12 that browser_act and browser_screenshot accept as a target. Refs are valid for the current document and until your next snapshot of it: after a navigation or a later snapshot, take a new snapshot before acting. The snapshot is cut at maxChars (default 24000, at most 64000) on a line boundary with a trailer saying how much was omitted and an outline of the page's landmarks and their refs, so you can call again with root set to a ref or a landmark role (banner, navigation, main, contentinfo, search, complementary, region, form) for one subtree; a rooted snapshot invalidates refs outside that subtree until the next whole-page snapshot. Returns the snapshot as text after a JSON header with the tab's URL, title and the cut.

tools.name: browser_act
tools.title: Browser act
tools.description: Act on an element in a MAWS browser tab: click, fill, select, check, press, hover or scroll; without this tool, ask the user to do it and tell you the result. target is a ref from browser_snapshot (e.g. "e12") or a locator {css, role?, name?} such as a comment anchor carries. fill types value into a field (replacing its content); select picks the option whose label or value is value; check sets a checkbox to value ("true" or "false", default true); press sends a key or chord (e.g. "Enter", "Control+a") to the element; scroll scrolls the element into view and then by value pixels when given (negative scrolls up). The action waits for the element to be visible and enabled (up to 10 s). If the user is using the page, the action waits until they stop or hand it back, and the result says so. A ref that no longer resolves is an error naming it: take a new snapshot. Returns the tab's URL and title after the action and whether it navigated.

tools.name: browser_eval
tools.title: Browser eval
tools.description: Evaluate a JavaScript expression in a MAWS browser tab's page and return its value; without this tool, use browser_snapshot or ask the user. Use it to read page state (text, attributes, computed values, JSON the page holds); it runs in the page with the page's permissions, so prefer browser_act for changes. A promise is awaited; the value is returned as JSON (cut at 16000 characters). If the user is using the page, the evaluation waits until they stop. Returns the value and the tab's URL and title.

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.title: Browser screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of a MAWS browser tab and receive it as an image; without this tool, use browser_snapshot. target (a ref or a locator) screenshots one element; fullPage captures the whole scrollable page; neither captures the viewport. The picture is also saved as a deliverable the user can open from the transcript. Pictures are kept under 3.5 MB (JPEG when a PNG would exceed it). Returns the image and a JSON record with the deliverable id, size and format.

message.content: Use the MAWS browser tools, calling each tool yourself, one after another, never through an agent. First call mcp__maws__browser_tabs with action "open" and url "http://127.0.0.1:17391/form.html" and note the tabId it returns. Then call mcp__maws__browser_snapshot on that tab and find the refs of the Name field, the Email field and the Submit button. Then call mcp__maws__browser_act with action "fill" on the Name field with value "Ada Lovelace", then mcp__maws__browser_act with action "fill" on the Email field with value "ada@example.test", then mcp__maws__browser_act with action "click" on the Submit button. The snapshot shows the Submit button as disabled, but the page enables it by itself once both fields are filled, so click it right after the second fill without taking another snapshot first. Then call mcp__maws__browser_snapshot again and read the reference number the page shows. Then call mcp__maws__browser_screenshot on the tab with no target. Reply with one line: the reference number exactly as shown, and the word "image" if you received a picture.
